interview.hardest_part: Maintaining the correct racing line through successive corners with delayed screenshots and one-second inputs, especially when the car is sliding or the camera orientation changes. Completing every stage without missing a checkpoint segment is substantially harder than merely moving forward.
interview.likely_failure: An early loss of control leaves the car off the road, spun around, or repeatedly automatically recovered, causing missed forward checkpoint passages. Even if early stages are completed, accumulated mistakes and thinking time are likely to prevent completion of all five stages within three hours.
interview.helpful_mechanics: The overhead view exposes much of the upcoming road, automatic transmission simplifies control, and there is no need to drive quickly or beat opponents because scoring rewards route progress. Automatic recovery, result navigation with Enter, per-segment scoring, and the ability to alternate gentle throttle with braking all support a cautious driving strategy.
interview.harmful_mechanics: The game continues while I deliberate, so stale screenshots and input latency can turn small steering errors into spins or collisions. One attempt, no manual recovery or restart, rally-car sliding physics, roadside obstacles, and the requirement for ordered forward checkpoint passage plus official finishes make errors costly. Five full stages also create substantial exposure to time exhaustion and repeated control mistakes.
